data.body_html:
When comparing the Mangusta 80 vs Sunseeker Predator 74 cost comparison Marbella 2043, the key difference is price: the Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for 4 hours with a free jet ski, while the Sunseeker Predator 74 typically costs €6,200+ for 4 hours with jet ski optional. Both boats offer premium experiences from Puerto Banús, but your choice depends on budget and desired layout. Read on for a detailed breakdown of costs, specs, and what’s included.

Mangusta 80 vs Sunseeker Predator 74: Key Specs

Cost Breakdown: Mangusta 80 Charter

The Mangusta 80 charter at €4,719 for 4 hours includes everything: a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% Spanish VAT. A jet ski is included free for the duration. For longer bookings, contact us via WhatsApp for custom rates. This makes it a cost-effective option for groups of up to 12 who want water sports without extra fees.

Cost Breakdown: Sunseeker Predator 74 Charter

The Sunseeker Predator 74 typically costs from €6,200 for 4 hours, depending on season and availability. This also includes skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT. However, a jet ski is usually an optional extra, adding €300–€500 per session. If you prioritise speed (36 knots) and an open sport deck, the Predator 74 delivers a different vibe, but at a higher base price.

Which Boat Offers Better Value?

For pure value, the Mangusta 80 wins on price per hour and included extras. At €1,180/hour (4h) with a free jet ski, it undercuts the Predator 74’s €1,550/hour (4h) plus jet ski cost. The flybridge layout on the Mangusta also provides shaded upper deck seating, ideal for Marbella’s 30°C summer days. The Predator 74’s open deck suits sunbathers and those who want a sportier ride.

Experience and Itinerary

Both boats depart from Puerto Banús, offering the same coastal routes: cruise past the Golden Mile, anchor at Cala del Faro, or head to Cabopino for lunch. The Mangusta 80’s flybridge gives panoramic views of La Concha mountain, while the Predator 74’s lower seating keeps you closer to the water. Both include soft drinks, beer, cava, and snacks, so the experience is similar—the main difference is the deck layout and speed.

When to Choose Each Boat

Choose the Mangusta 80 if you want a flybridge, a free jet ski, and a lower cost—perfect for families or groups who want water sports. Choose the Sunseeker Predator 74 if you value top speed (36 knots), an open sport deck, and don’t mind paying extra for a jet ski. For a balanced option, the Mangusta 80 offers more for less.
